info.title: Alacart API
info.description:
# Getting started

The Alacart API lets your app read and change a user's shopping lists, items, recipe box and meal
plan, and read the user's stores. Your app acts for one user at a time, and that user must have premium. The user signs in to
Alacart and approves your app, so your app never sees their password.

To call the API, follow these steps:

1. Register your app on the developer page of the Alacart web app, which the profile page links
   to. Registering an app needs premium. Each app gets a client id, which works only in the
   environment where you registered it. Choose a confidential app when it runs on a server that
   can keep a secret. It also gets a client secret, and the page shows the secret only once. Choose
   a public app for a mobile app, a browser app or a script. Both kinds sign in with PKCE.
2. Sign the user in with the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow and PKCE.
   [Signing in](#description/signing-in) shows each request.
3. Send each call with the access token in the `Authorization` header.

```sh
curl https://api.alacart.io/v1/item-lists \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

## Hosts

The API has two hosts:

- `https://api.alacart.io` will serve the users of the app once the API launches there. Until
  then, the beta host alone serves it.
- `https://api.test.alacart.io` is the beta host, with its own accounts and data. Test your app there,
  with a beta account that the Alacart team has given premium.

Users sign in to your app at an authorization server of the same environment. It is
`https://auth.alacart.io` for production and `https://auth.test.alacart.io` for beta. A token from
one environment does not work in the other. The examples use the production hosts.

## Conventions

- Every path starts with `/v1/`.
- Ids are JSON strings. Treat them as opaque text, even when they look like numbers.
- JSON names are camelCase. Values that come from a fixed list, such as an error code or a sort
  order, are snake_case.
- Timestamps are UTC in the RFC 3339 format with whole seconds, such as `2026-10-25T07:21:39Z`.
- A collection comes wrapped in an object, as in `{ "items": [...] }`.
- Some fields cost more to compute, or few apps need them. An answer carries such a field only when
  the request names it in the `include` parameter, as in `include=ingredients`. The reference marks
  these fields as optional.
- Every other field is always there. A value the API does not know is `null`.
- `GET /v1/item-lists` and `GET /v1/items` send an `ETag` header. Send it back in `If-None-Match`,
  and an answer that has not changed comes back as `304 Not Modified` without a body.
- Browsers on every origin may call the API, without cookies.

## Changing data

Endpoints that change data need the `write` scope, which
[Scopes and consent](#description/scopes-and-consent) describes. They follow these rules:

- A request sends its body as JSON, with `Content-Type: application/json`. A body may hold at most
  64 KB, which is 65,536 bytes.
- `PATCH` changes only the fields that the body holds, and keeps the others. The body must hold at
  least one field.
- An answer that creates a list, a recipe or meals is `201 Created` with what it created.
  `POST /v1/items` answers `200 OK`, because a text can merge into an item already on the list.
- An answer to `DELETE`, and to a change that returns nothing, is `204 No Content` without a body.
- `POST /v1/items` and `POST /v1/meal-plans/active/meals` take several entries in one call. They
  check every entry before they add any. A list can still fill up partway, and the problem then
  lists what the call added, as [Errors](#description/errors) describes.
- A `POST` can have gone through even when the app got no answer, or got `server_error`. Read the
  data again before you repeat it, because a repeated text adds to the item it merged into.
- Deleting a list or a recipe cannot be undone.

This call adds two items to the user's default list:

```sh
curl https://api.alacart.io/v1/items \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "texts": ["2 l mjölk", "bananer"] }'
```

The body takes up to 50 texts, and `listId` picks another list than the default one. The API
merges a text into an item already on the list when the two name the same thing. The answer holds
one entry per text, and each entry's `mergedIntoExisting` says whether its text merged.

# Signing in

Your app gets its tokens through the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE. Every app uses
PKCE, whether it has a client secret or not. The authorization server has a host of its own, apart
from the API:

| Environment | Authorization server | API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Production | `https://auth.alacart.io` | `https://api.alacart.io` |
| Beta | `https://auth.test.alacart.io` | `https://api.test.alacart.io` |

The examples use the production hosts. The authorization server publishes its endpoints at
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, which is
`https://auth.test.alacart.io/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` on beta. An OAuth library can
read them from there.

## Send the user to the authorization endpoint

Create a random code verifier, and derive its S256 code challenge. Then open this address in the
user's browser:

```
https://auth.alacart.io/connect/authorize
  ?response_type=code
  &client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
  &redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI
  &scope=read%20write
  &code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE
  &code_challenge_method=S256
  &state=RANDOM_STATE
```

The parameters work like this:

- `redirect_uri` must be one of the redirect URIs you registered for the app. An app may register
  a loopback URI, such as `http://127.0.0.1/callback`, a URI with its own app scheme, or an HTTPS
  URI. For a loopback URI, your app may listen on any port.
- `scope` is `read`, or `read write` when the app needs to change anything.
  [Scopes and consent](#description/scopes-and-consent) explains the difference.
- `state` is a random value that your app checks when the browser comes back.
- `resource` is optional. When you send it, it must be the API's address with `/v1`, which is
  `https://api.alacart.io/v1` in production and `https://api.test.alacart.io/v1` in beta.

The user signs in, if they have not already, and approves your app. The browser then comes back to
your redirect URI with `code` and `state` in the query. When the user declines, or cannot approve
because their account has no premium, it comes back with `error=access_denied`.

## Exchange the code for tokens

Send the code to the token endpoint, with the code verifier:

```sh
curl https://auth.alacart.io/connect/token \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d code=CODE \
  -d redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d code_verifier=CODE_VERIFIER
```

An app with a client secret also sends it. It may use HTTP Basic authentication, or put
`client_secret` in the form body.

The answer holds an `access_token`, which lives 60 minutes, and a `refresh_token`. Every sign-in
comes with a refresh token, so your app does not need to ask for `offline_access`.

## Refresh the access token

Before the access token expires, ask for a new one:

```sh
curl https://auth.alacart.io/connect/token \
  -d grant_type=refresh_token \
  -d refresh_token=REFRESH_TOKEN \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
```

Each refresh returns a new refresh token. The old one keeps working for 30 seconds, so an app that
lost the answer can retry, and then it stops. Store the new one every time. A refresh token lives 90 days from the refresh that issued it. An app that keeps running
refreshes at least once an hour, so its user signs in again only after the app has been off for 90
days.

When a call answers `invalid_token`, refresh the token and try again. When the refresh fails, sign
the user in again.

## Sign the user out

To sign the user out of your app, revoke its refresh token:

```sh
curl https://auth.alacart.io/connect/revoke \
  -d token=REFRESH_TOKEN \
  -d token_type_hint=refresh_token \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
```

Your app can then no longer refresh. The access token keeps working until it expires, at most 60
minutes later, so delete it too.

Revoking the refresh token does not disconnect your app from the user's account, and the app stays
on the profile page of the Alacart web app. Only the user can disconnect it, on that page. Its
tokens then stop working at once.

# Scopes and consent

The API has two scopes:

- `read` lets the app read the user's lists, items, favorites, recipes, meal plan and stores.
- `write` lets the app read everything that `read` allows, and change it.

The reference names the scope that each endpoint needs. An endpoint that reads takes either scope,
and an endpoint that changes data needs `write`.

When your app asks for `write`, the consent page shows the user a choice to allow changes. A user
who turns it off approves `read` alone. Your app will then get an answer with the code
`insufficient_scope` whenever it tries to change anything. Read the scope in the token endpoint's
answer, and offer the user a way to sign in again when your app needs `write`.

The consent page names your app and the host of your redirect URI. It also tells the user that
nobody at Alacart has reviewed your app.

Only an account with premium can approve an app. When the user's premium ends later, the app stays
connected, and every call answers `premium_required` until the user renews it. Signing in again does
not help, so show the user the reason.

The user can disconnect your app at any time. Its tokens then stop working, and every call answers
`invalid_token`.

# Errors

Every error answer is a problem, as RFC 9457 defines it, with the media type
`application/problem+json`:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.alacart.io/docs#errors-not_found",
  "title": "The resource does not exist.",
  "status": 404,
  "code": "not_found",
  "detail": "The user has no item list with id 42."
}
```

A problem carries four of the five standard members of RFC 9457:

- `type` links to the code's description below.
- `title` describes the code in a few words. It is the same for every answer with that code.
- `status` repeats the HTTP status.
- `detail` describes this answer, for a developer to read.

The fifth, `instance`, never appears, because the API does not name the failed request.

`title` and `detail` are not meant for your users.

The API adds extension members, which RFC 9457 allows:

- `code` comes with every problem. Branch on it, because it never changes once it ships.
- `errors` comes with `invalid_request` when the request got a parameter or a body field wrong.
  Each key names one, and its value lists what is wrong with it. A key names an entry of an array
  by its index, as in `texts[2]` or `meals[1].portions`. An answer whose fault no single parameter
  or field carries has no `errors`.
- `limit` comes with `limit_reached`, and gives the most items a list may hold.
- `items` comes with `limit_reached` from `POST /v1/items`. It lists the entries that the call
  added before the list filled up, which can be none.
- `meals` comes with `limit_reached` from `POST /v1/meal-plans/active/meals`. It lists every meal
  that the call put in the plan. That includes the meal whose ingredients filled the list, which
  keeps the ingredients added before the list filled.
- `reason` comes with `recipe_import_failed`, and says why the API could not add the recipe.

`invalid_request` with `errors` looks like this:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.alacart.io/docs#errors-invalid_request",
  "title": "The request is not valid.",
  "status": 400,
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "detail": "The limit must be from 1 to 100.",
  "errors": {
    "limit": ["The limit must be from 1 to 100."]
  }
}
```

Later releases may add codes and members. Treat a code you do not know by its HTTP status.

## Error codes

### invalid_request

Status 400. A parameter or body field is missing or invalid. `errors` names the one the API found,
when it can single one out. A body can hold more faults than the answer names, so fix the request
before you send it again.

### invalid_token

Status 401. The token is missing, expired or revoked. A token for another API, or for an account
that no longer exists, gets it too. The `WWW-Authenticate` header says the same. Refresh the token,
or sign the user in again when the refresh fails.

### insufficient_scope

Status 403. The token's scopes do not allow the call, such as a change when the user allowed
reading only. The `WWW-Authenticate` header names the scope `write`. Signing the user in again,
with `write` in the request, lets the user allow changes.

### premium_required

Status 403. The account has no premium. The user can renew it in the app, and signing in again does
not help.

### not_found

Status 404. The id does not exist, or it belongs to another user, or the path does not exist. An id
that the API never issued, such as `abc`, gets it too.

### method_not_allowed

Status 405. The path does not take that method. The `Allow` header lists the methods it takes.

### payload_too_large

Status 413. The body is larger than 64 KB, which is 65,536 bytes. Split the change into smaller
calls.

### unsupported_media_type

Status 415. The body is not JSON. Send it with `Content-Type: application/json`.

### limit_reached

Status 409. The list holds as many items as it may, and `limit` says how many. A call that adds
several entries may have added some before the list filled up, and `items` or `meals` lists them.
A change of a meal's portions can also fill the list. Its problem carries neither member, so read
the meal plan again to see what changed. The user removes items before the app adds more.

Read the members of `limit_reached` to tell the user what the call did before the list filled
up:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.alacart.io/docs#errors-limit_reached",
  "title": "The list is full.",
  "status": 409,
  "code": "limit_reached",
  "detail": "The list is full. A list can hold at most 200 items.",
  "limit": 200,
  "items": []
}
```

### conflict

Status 409. The change clashes with the user's own data. These changes get it:

- a list with the name of another of the user's lists;
- deleting the account's last shared list, or making it private;
- making a list that another person shares with the user visible to the account;
- deleting a recipe with a meal in the active meal plan, or a meal the user cooked in the last
  few days.

### recipe_import_failed

Status 422. The API could not add the recipe on the web page. `reason` is one of these:

- `site_not_supported`: the API does not add recipes from that site.
- `site_denies_import`: the recipe site does not allow the API to add its recipes.
- `unreadable_page`: the page's HTML is broken, so the API cannot read it.
- `multiple_recipes_found`: the page has more than one recipe.
- `no_recipe_found`: the API found no recipe on the page.
- `other`: the API could not read the recipe for another reason.

Later releases may add reasons. Treat a reason you do not know as `other`.

### rate_limited

Status 429. Your app sent too many requests. Wait the number of seconds that `Retry-After` gives.
[Rate limits](#description/rate-limits) describes the limits.

### server_error

Status 500. The API failed. Try again later.

### unavailable

Status 503. A service that the call needs is down or slow. Wait the number of seconds that
`Retry-After` gives.

# Rate limits

Each user may make 60 requests a minute through your app. Design your app to make as few requests as it can, and to fetch only what it
needs. The limit is a maximum, not a budget to use up. Alacart may lower it if apps use too much.

Two more limits guard the API against bursts:

- One token may make 6 requests a second, after a burst of 30.
- One IP address may make 60 requests a second.

A request over any of these limits gets the code `rate_limited` and a `Retry-After` header, which
says how many seconds to wait. Every request counts, also one that gets `304 Not Modified`.

These habits keep an app well within the limits:

- Poll no more often than you need. Shopping lists change slowly, and once every few minutes is
  enough for a list on a screen.
- Send the last `ETag` in `If-None-Match`. An answer that has not changed then costs no body.
- Read every list's items with one call to `GET /v1/items`. Prefer to pass `listId` when you
  show a single list, so the API loads that list alone.
- Ask for item suggestions only when the user pauses typing, because each call counts.
- Add several items with one call to `POST /v1/items`, and plan several meals with one call to
  `POST /v1/meal-plans/active/meals`.

# Versioning

Version 1 of the API lives under `/v1/`. It changes only in ways that keep existing apps working.
A later release of v1 may add any of these:

- new endpoints;
- new optional parameters;
- new response fields;
- new values of a field with fixed values, such as a meal's `type`;
- new error codes and problem members.

Your app must ignore a field it does not know. It must also handle a value it does not know
without failing, for example by skipping that entry.

A change that would break an app goes into a new version under `/v2/`. Version 1 then keeps
running for at least six months. Its answers carry a `Deprecation` header, and a `Sunset` header
with the date it stops.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: Optional. Narrows the answer to one list. Without it, the answer holds the items of every list.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Optional. `added`, the default, puts the most recently added items first. `manual` follows the order the user set by hand, and needs `listId`.

post.summary: Adds items to a shopping list.
post.description:
The API merges a text into an item already on the list when the two name the same
thing. The endpoint checks every text before it adds any. When the list fills up
partway, the answer is `limit_reached`, and its `items` member lists the entries added
before that. Scope: `write`.

get.description: The app can suggest them when the user adds items. Scope: `read`.

get.description:
The suggestions come in the order the suggestion service ranks them. Each call counts
against the rate limit, so an app should wait until the user pauses typing. Scope: `read`.

parameters.description: Required. From 1 to 100 characters.

patch.description:
A name that another list has gets `conflict`. Two changes of `isPrivate` get `conflict`
too: making a list that another person shares with the user visible to the account, and
making the account's last shared list private. Scope: `write`.

parameters.description: The list's id.

delete.summary: Deletes one of the user's shopping lists, with its items.
delete.description:
For a list that another person shares with the user, it removes the list from the
user's lists and leaves it to its owner. When the deleted list was the default list,
another list becomes the default. A deleted list cannot be restored. The last list that
the account shares cannot be deleted, even when the user has private lists, and gets
`conflict`. Scope: `write`.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: The list's id.

put.summary: Sets the order of a list's items by hand, as the user does in the apps.
put.description:
`GET /v1/items` with `order=manual` then returns the items in this order. Items that the
body leaves out, and items added later, have no place in the order, and come first. An
item id from another list gets `not_found`, and a repeated id gets `invalid_request`.
Scope: `write`.

parameters.name: listId
parameters.description: The list's id.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`: The user allowed reading only. `premium_required`: The account has no premium.

patch.description:
A field left out keeps its value. The `ETag` of `GET /v1/items` changes whenever its
answer changes. A check through the API carries no position or store, so it does not
influence how the user's stores sort the list. Scope: `write`.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The item's id.

get.description:
Without a query, tags or filters, it returns the whole recipe box, one page at a time.
The order of recipes that tie under a sort order is not part of the contract, so two
calls can split ties differently at a page boundary. Scope: `read`.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Optional. Words to search for, in Swedish.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Optional. Every recipe must have each tag. Repeat the parameter for each tag, as in `tags=vegetariskt` and `tags=snabbt` in one request.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Optional. The default is `relevance`, which puts the best match first when there is a query,
and the newest recipe first when there is none. `newest` puts the most recently added recipe
first, and `alphabetical` sorts by title. `most_cooked` and `least_cooked` sort by how many
times the user has cooked the recipe. `latest_cooked` and `earliest_cooked` sort by when the
user last cooked it, and put recipes the user has never cooked last. `shortest_cooking_time`
puts recipes without a known time last. `highest_grade` sorts by the user's grade, puts
recipes without a grade last, and puts the most cooked first among equal grades. `random`
gives a new order on each call, so `offset` does not page through it.

parameters.name: maxCookingTime
parameters.description: Optional. At least 1. Keeps the recipes that take at most this many minutes, and leaves out recipes without a known time.

parameters.name: minGrade
parameters.description: Optional. From 1 to 5. Keeps the recipes the user graded at least this high.

parameters.name: cooked
parameters.description: Optional. True keeps the recipes the user has cooked, and false the ones the user has never cooked.

parameters.name: ownRecipesOnly
parameters.description: Optional. True keeps the recipes written in the app by the user or by someone who shares the recipe box.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Optional. From 1 to 100. The default is 50.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Optional. At least 0. The default is 0.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Optional. `cookCount`, `lastCookedAt` or both, separated by a comma.

`conflict`, so the app removes the meal first. A recipe whose meal the user cooked
within the last few days can get `conflict` too. Scope: `write`.

get.summary: Returns a recipe's ingredients for a number of portions, with each item once.

post.summary: Downloads the recipe on a web page and adds it to the recipe box.
post.description:
The answer is `201` when the recipe is new, and `200` when the recipe box already held
it. When the API cannot add the recipe, the answer is `recipe_import_failed`, and its
`reason` member says why: `site_not_supported`, `site_denies_import`,
`unreadable_page`, `multiple_recipes_found`, `no_recipe_found` or `other`. Later
releases may add reasons. When the recipe downloader is down or the site does not answer
in time, the answer is `unavailable`. Scope: `write`.

401.description: `invalid_token`: The access token is not valid.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`: The user allowed reading only. `premium_required`: The account has no premium.

422.description: `recipe_import_failed`: The recipe could not be added.

429.description: `rate_limited`: The app sent too many requests.

503.description: `unavailable`: A service that the call needs is unavailable.

post.summary: Adds meals to the active meal plan, and adds each meal's chosen ingredients to a shopping list.
post.description:
The endpoint checks every meal before it adds any. It then adds the meals one at a time,
and for each meal it saves the meal first and adds the ingredients after. When the list
fills up partway, the answer is `limit_reached`, and its `meals` member lists every meal
the call put in the plan. That includes the meal whose ingredients filled the list, which
keeps the ingredients added before the list filled. Another failure partway, such as
`server_error`, can also leave some meals in the plan, so the app reads the meal plan
again before it repeats the call. Scope: `write`.

401.description: `invalid_token`: The access token is not valid.

403.description: `insufficient_scope`: The user allowed reading only. `premium_required`: The account has no premium.

429.description: `rate_limited`: The app sent too many requests.

patch.summary: Changes a meal in the active meal plan.
patch.description:
The id of a meal the user has cooked gets `not_found`. A larger portion count can need
new items, and a full list then gets `limit_reached`. The change can then be partly
done, so the app should read the meal plan again. Scope: `write`.

parameters.description: The meal's id.

delete.summary: Removes a meal from the active meal plan.
delete.description:
The API also takes back what it added to the shopping list for the meal, and the recipe
stays in the recipe box. The id of a meal the user has cooked gets `not_found`. Scope:
`write`.
